sources.quote: Console sketch showing the dimensions of the XBOX Series X with disc drive: Height is 301 mm, depth is 151mm and breadth is 151mm

sources.method: 9.8 lb (sources[1], xbox.com 'Weight 9.8 lbs.') x 453.59237 g/lb = 4445.2 g, rounded to the gram: 4445

sources.quote: With XBOX Series X, an XBOX Series X console, controller, Ultra High Speed HDMI cable, and power cord are included.

notes: xbox.com Series X page, 'DESIGN > Disc' block, read from the raw HTML on 2026-11-01. The axis labels come from the sketch's alt text (Height 301 mm, depth 151 mm, breadth 151 mm), which is the console standing up, so the figure is filed as the 'vertical' state per the home-console contract; 'breadth' is recorded as width. The visible line beside it reads 'Dimensions 15.1cm x 15.1cm x 30.1cm' (unlabelled, consistent). No 'body' (lying-down) state is published; it is left out rather than rotated by us. The page does not say whether projections are excluded: excludes_projections null.
Mass: xbox.com publishes pounds only; mass_g is a derived conversion (factor 453.59237 g/lb), not a maker gram figure.
Uncovered on purpose: media (the spec table says 'Optical Drive. XBOX Series X Carbon Black: 4K UHD Blu-Ray' but not whether it is a slot or a tray).
The same page also lists 'XBOX Series X – 1TB Digital Edition' and '2TB Galaxy Black Special Edition'; the digital edition is its own object (microsoft-xbox-series-x-all-digital).
external_ids: Wikidata Q64513817 confirmed through the Wikidata API; igdb_platform 'series-x' is Wikidata's P5795 on that item.

ports: the maker's 'PORTS & CONNECTIVITY' block, filed as its complete list: hdmi 1, usb_a 3, ethernet 1. usb_a is our mapping of the maker's 'USB 3.1 Gen 1 ports' (no plug type named), per the coordinator ruling of 2026-11-01. Not in that block and therefore not filed: the power inlet (a 'power cord' is in the box contents) and the 'dedicated storage expansion port' that the page's FAQ mentions.
